candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is gastric schwannoma. GIST is a separate spindle-cell tumor of the stomach arising from interstitial cells of Cajal (c-KIT/PDGFRA-driven), whereas schwannoma arises from Schwann cells (S-100 positive, c-KIT negative). Although both are hypoechoic muscularis propria masses on EUS and the radiologist initially suggested GIST, the clinical features (calcification on FNA, lack of internal vascularity, smooth margins, surrounding reactive lymphadenopathy typical of schwannoma) point away from GIST. GIST and schwannoma share anatomical location and imaging overlap but are immunohistochemically and biologically distinct subtypes; asserting GIST conflicts with the schwannoma reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: GIST is a distinct mesenchymal tumor subtype incompatible with schwannoma as the reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: EUS-FNA was non-diagnostic; definitive diagnosis would require surgical resection with immunohistochemistry (S-100, CD117, DOG1)
Surrounding lymphadenopathy is a recognized feature of gastric schwannoma and helps differentiate it from GIST
